title: A Passage for the Current
premise: Ada Quintana, a railroad engineer haunted by the closed mountain lines her late father surveyed, is hired to find a vanished government survey team in the Cordillera del Viento. With her estranged brother Tomás, a disgraced cartographer, and a guide who once loved her, she discovers the team was erased by a mining consortium that wants the pass sealed and the records buried. Racing the first snows and the brief glacier-calving window that opens the high route, Ada must choose between destroying her father's map — the last proof of the pass's existence — or using it to expose the truth. She crosses ahead of the calving ice, buries the map in the river it was drawn for, and lets the wilderness keep its secret while carrying the memory of everyone the mountains took.
about_author: Paloma Oyelaran is a former hydrologist who spent six years mapping seasonal waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that outlast the people who try to name them.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Ada Quintana, POV. In a rail office in Puerto Frío, Ada receives a government contract to locate the missing Delgado survey team along the abandoned northern lines. Her father's old map of closed routes hums with memory and guilt. Emotional beat: reluctant duty stirring an old wound.

chapters.title: Gear Without Tracks
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. At the last known campsite she finds intact tents, instruments still running, food unspoiled — and no footprints beyond the treeline. The absence reads as violence without a body. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Brother's Fault Lines
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. Ada recruits Tomás, now drinking away his cartography license in a border town. Their father's death split them; the map is the wedge between them. He agrees for reasons he won't say aloud. Emotional beat: bitterness laced with longing.

chapters.title: The Guide Who Waited
chapters.summary: Río, POV. Río Salazar, who guided Ada's father on his final survey and once loved Ada, agrees to lead them upriver. He warns them the glacier route opens only during calving season — days, not weeks. Emotional beat: tenderness guarded by grief.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Following the river north, they find a surveyor's notebook wedged in stones — Delgado's handwriting, growing frantic, naming a company: Consorcio Andrade. Someone else is reading over their shoulders at night. Emotional beat: the hunt becomes a being-hunted.

chapters.title: Smoke on the Ridgeline
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. They spot a second expedition moving parallel — armed men flying no flag. Tomás recognizes the consortium's survey marks from his disgrace years ago; he was paid to falsify maps for them once. Emotional beat: shame surfacing as urgency.

chapters.title: The First Snows Come Early
chapters.summary: Río, POV. Weather turns; the low passes begin closing. They must commit to the high glacier route before calving season or winter here forever. A mule is lost, and with it half their provisions. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into discipline.

chapters.title: Delgado's Last Camp
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. They find the team's forward camp ransacked but one survivor's cache hidden in a crevasse: photographs proving Andrade dynamited a rail tunnel to hide mineral seams under the pass. Emotional beat: vindication entangled with dread.

chapters.title: Bargain at the Timberline
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. The rival party catches them at the timberline. Their leader, Vásquez, offers safe passage down if Ada surrenders the map. She refuses; Tomás nearly takes the deal. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against self-preservation.

chapters.title: Icefall Crossing
chapters.summary: Río, POV. The party ropes together and crosses the icefall at dawn, when frost bonds the seracs. A rope snaps; Río saves Tomás at cost of his own hand badly frostbitten. Emotional beat: sacrifice quietly rewriting old debts.

chapters.title: The Calving Window Opens
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The glacier calves, thundering open the high corridor — forty-eight hours of passage. But Vásquez's men are behind them, and the weather window is shrinking faster than promised. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by the clock.

chapters.title: What My Father Found
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. In a frozen shelter, Tomás finds their father's final journal: he discovered the seam, refused Andrade's money, and died for it — not by accident, as Ada believes. Tomás must decide whether to tell her. Emotional beat: truth as both burden and gift.

chapters.title: The Telling
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Tomás confesses everything — the murder, his own falsified maps, his years of silence. Ada's fury nearly breaks the party apart on the ice. Emotional beat: love against duty, duty losing ground.

chapters.title: Vásquez Closes In
chapters.summary: Río, POV. The consortium men gain on them through the corridor, shooting to disable rather than kill — they need witnesses eliminated cleanly, not martyrs. Río rigs a false trail toward a cornice. Emotional beat: cunning born of desperation.

chapters.title: The Cornice Gives Way
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The trap works too well: two pursuers die, and Vásquez, enraged, stops pretending. A storm front swallows the corridor early. The calving window is closing with them inside it. Emotional beat: triumph curdling into survival.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. Lost in the whiteout, roped blind, they navigate by river-sound alone — Ada's engineering ear reading the current beneath the ice. They find the lower exit chute minutes before it seals. Emotional beat: trust rebuilt in the dark, literally.

chapters.title: The Pass Above the World
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. They emerge onto the summit shelf where her father stood last. From here she can see the whole secret range — and the consortium's staging camp below, waiting for spring. The map could destroy them all or save the valley. Emotional beat: awe braided with responsibility.

chapters.title: Terms of the Descent
chapters.summary: Río, POV. Vásquez corners them at the descent with rifles and reason: give up the map, walk away rich. Río counters with the one thing Vásquez fears — the calving season itself, which will erase every trace by morning. Emotional beat: negotiation as a knife held level.

chapters.title: The River Decides
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Climax. Rather than surrender or hoard it, Ada commits her father's map to the meltwater torrent — the river it was drawn for — letting the current carry the truth somewhere no company can buy. Vásquez lunges; the ice edge fails beneath him. Emotional beat: release, terrible and clean.

chapters.title: What Survives the Season
chapters.summary: Tomás, POV. They descend through the closing corridor as the glacier seals the pass behind them. Tomás carries not the map but his testimony — sworn, witnessed, enough to reopen the investigation from the lowlands. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Passage for the Current
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Home in Puerto Frío, Ada files the report, buries her father beside the rail line he loved, and stands with Tomás and Río as the first honest trains in twenty years are scheduled north. The pass stays closed; the people do not. Emotional beat: quiet restoration.

chapters.title: Coda: What the Wilderness Remembers
chapters.summary: Río, POV. Years later, Río guides a young surveyor past the sealed range and tells her only what the river allows. Somewhere under the ice, the map travels on. Some things are kept better than found. Emotional beat: peace with what cannot be recovered.
